title: Plan says preserve a signature, but no arithmetic.py exists
desc: The plan says 'Preserve this public signature' for add(a, b) in arithmetic.py, which implies an existing module. The repository has no arithmetic.py and no other .py file (checked the repo root and find over the tree), so there is nothing to preserve. The implementer cannot tell whether to create the module or modify one elsewhere. The plan should state that arithmetic.py is new, or name the existing file and its current signature.
scope_reason: Resolves the plan's own instruction about the file it asks to change; adds no new work.
scope_reference: Plan line 3: 'Implement add(a, b) returning a+b in arithmetic.py ... Preserve this public signature.'

title: Signature is only partly given; operand types are undefined
desc: The plan names add(a, b) but gives no type expectations for a and b and no return type. 'Returning a+b' for ints gives an int, for floats a float, and for strings a concatenation, and the plan does not say which inputs are supported. It also does not say what happens for non-numeric inputs such as None or str, or whether bool is accepted. The 'preserve this public signature' requirement cannot be checked without this. The plan should state the supported types, the behaviour for unsupported types (raise TypeError, or pass through to Python's +), and whether mixed int/float is in scope.
scope_reason: Defines the behaviour the plan already requires for add(a, b); it adds no capability.

title: Test file location and run command are not specified
desc: The plan says to 'Verify positive, negative and zero operands with unittest', but it does not name the test file, its location, or how it is run (for example python -m unittest, or a discover pattern). Without that, the verification step has no defined target and nothing in the plan says the tests must be runnable from the repository root. The plan should give the test file path and the exact command.
scope_reason: Specifies how the unittest verification the plan already asks for is run.
scope_reference: Plan line 3: 'Verify positive, negative and zero operands with unittest.'

title: No acceptance criterion for the verification step
desc: The plan lists the operand classes to verify but gives no pass criterion. It does not say that all unittest cases must pass, or that add must return the exact sum for each class. It also does not say what counts as 'zero operands': both zero, or one zero and one non-zero. These cases can be read differently, so the implementer cannot tell when the work is done. The plan should state the acceptance condition, such as all cases pass with exact results, and enumerate the zero cases.
scope_reason: Adds the pass condition for the testing the plan already requires.
scope_reference: Plan line 3: 'Verify positive, negative and zero operands with unittest.'

title: Plan lacks problem statement, objectives and file change list
desc: The plan is a single sentence. It has no problem statement or objective (why add is needed, or what consumes it), no list of file changes (the new or changed arithmetic.py and a test file), and no description of the architecture or the stdlib-only constraint's scope. The plan is expected to contain these sections. Without the file list an implementer does not know whether to touch any file besides arithmetic.py, and the stdlib-only requirement is stated without saying what it covers (the implementation, the tests, or both).
scope_reason: Fills in the plan sections the review expects; it does not add a feature.
